I'm from Ireland and the last few days have been really grinding my gears to say the least.

For those unaware, the Irish government held a referendum on friday to amend the constitution to allow for gay marriage. The constitution never actually forbade it, so the whole thing was of questionable value, but it's been a long time in the coming and a few hours ago the numbers finally came in and the answer is "yes."

I've no problem with gay marriage, I used to actively campaign for it, but my social network sites are being flooded with messages from all my friends fawning over each other for having had the grace to permit consenting adults to form a family. I mean... I get that it's great, people's lives will improve because they get to fit into that cubbyhole the government made for them... but I'm not seeing anyone questioning the value behind something like this going to a vote in the first place.

It also boggles me that a country which owes it's existence to an undemocratic secession from an unwilling union can be so statist.

Spot on, mate. I'm a bigot who has a religious problem with non-hetero relationships, but why should I expect to use the force of government to prevent others from choosing how to run their lives?

Congrats, Ireland. You've voted to allow yourselves permission to conduct a specific sort of consensual arrangement that really shouldn't have been an affair of the state to begin with.
That's a great step in the right direction.
